Buñuelos

Served at: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Serves 8-10Prep 20 minCook 15 min

Buñuelos are a traditional Mexican fried pastry that are especially popular during the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th. These crispy, golden treats are often sprinkled with cinnamon sugar and enjoyed as a festive dessert or snack, symbolizing warmth and celebration during the holiday season.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups all-purpose flour (250 g)
  • 1 tablespoon baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 2 tablespoons sugar
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, softened
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1/2 cup whole milk (120 ml)
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • Vegetable oil for frying (about 4 cups / 1 liter)
  • 1/2 cup granulated sugar (100 g)
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon

Method

  1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar.
  2. Add the softened butter and mix with your fingers or a pastry cutter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
  3. In a separate bowl, beat the eggs with the milk and vanilla extract.
  4. Gradually add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, mixing until a soft dough forms.
  5. Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead gently for about 3-4 minutes until smooth.
  6. Divide the dough into 12 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
  7. Using a rolling pin, roll each ball into a thin circle about 6 inches (15 cm) in diameter.
  8. Heat the vegetable oil in a deep skillet or frying pan over medium-high heat until it reaches 350°F (175°C).
  9. Fry the dough circles one or two at a time, flipping once, until golden and puffed, about 1-2 minutes per side.
  10. Remove the buñuelos with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
  11. Mix the granulated sugar and cinnamon in a shallow bowl.
  12. While still warm, sprinkle or dip each buñuelo in the cinnamon sugar mixture to coat evenly.
  13. Serve warm and enjoy!

Tips

  • For a thinner, crispier buñuelo, roll the dough as thinly as possible without tearing.
  • You can substitute milk with water for a lighter dough.
  • Add a splash of orange blossom water or anise extract to the dough for extra traditional flavor.
